_about: Curated seed list for Wayward Bike. Each destination is one of two kinds. kind=base: a town you stay in and ride out from. offers = what you can ride from it, by discipline: mtb: lift (lifts & shuttles), trails (trail centres and natural trails) · road: day, climbs, cobbles · gravel: day. category = its main discipline (sets the dot colour). kind=route: a multi-day route, one-way or loop (you move on each night); category = main surface; support = hotel | bikepacking | remote. season/best are month numbers (season wraps if start > end). elev = [low, high] m; refElev = where riding conditions are modelled. stats: km, days, climb (m) for routes. children = a few highlights (not every ride): kind area | park | climb | section, with a short note.

destinations.name: Moab
destinations.airport: Grand Junction ~2 h, Salt Lake City ~4 h, Las Vegas ~6.5 h
destinations.terrain: Slickrock, ledges and desert singletrack; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Red-rock desert riding on grippy sandstone, from the famous Slickrock loop to the Whole Enchilada, a big descent from alpine meadows to the Colorado River.

children.name: Slickrock Trail
children.note: ~17 km loop on bare sandstone; steep, technical, iconic

children.name: Whole Enchilada
children.note: ~42 km, ~2,400 m descent from Burro Pass to the river (shuttle); advanced; opens ~June up top

children.name: Captain Ahab
children.note: Climb Amasa Back, then a ledgy slickrock descent above the Colorado; ~15 km loop; advanced

children.name: Klondike Bluffs
children.note: Flowy beginner–intermediate singletrack north of town; dinosaur tracks

children.name: Mag 7
children.note: Linked rim trails with big canyon views (Gemini Bridges, Portal); intermediate–expert

children.name: Navajo Rocks & Brand
children.note: Mellow-to-mid desert loops; good first days

destinations.hireNote: Lots of shops with high-end full-suspension bikes; book ahead in spring and autumn

destinations.name: Whistler
destinations.airport: Vancouver ~2 h by road (Sea to Sky Highway)
destinations.terrain: Lift-served bike park and valley singletrack; all levels, very steep at the top end
destinations.pitch: The world's best-known bike park, with 70+ lift-served trails from beginner flow to pro jump lines, plus a huge network of hand-built valley singletrack.

children.name: Whistler Mountain Bike Park
children.note: ~1,500 m lift-served vertical, 70+ trails; Top of the World opens mid-summer

children.name: Lost Lake
children.note: Beginner-friendly cross-country loops beside the village

children.name: Westside & Comfortably Numb
children.note: Rooty, rocky BC-style tech; Comfortably Numb is a ~25 km classic

destinations.hireNote: Bike-park and trail bikes all over the village

destinations.name: Squamish
destinations.terrain: Steep granite slabs, roots and loamy forest; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Steep, technical forest trails on granite between Vancouver and Whistler. Locals call it the 'Sea to Sky' style: roll-ins, slabs and roots.

children.name: Diamond Head / Garibaldi Highlands
children.note: Classic tech: Half Nelson, Pseudo-Tsuga

children.name: Alice Lake
children.note: Mellower loops and family riding

destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting good trail bikes

destinations.name: Sedona
destinations.terrain: Red-rock singletrack with ledges and exposure; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Desert singletrack among red-rock spires, with famous exposed lines like Hiline and Hangover. A winter and shoulder-season classic when the mountains are snowed in.
destinations.weather: Summer is very hot; July–September also brings monsoon storms.

children.name: Hiline & Slim Shady
children.note: South-side loops: flowy Slim Shady, exposed Hiline

children.name: Hangover & Munds Wagon
children.note: Cliffside slickrock; expert, with real exposure

children.name: West Sedona (Thunder Mountain)
children.note: Close-to-town tech loops

destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting high-end trail bikes

destinations.name: Bentonville
destinations.terrain: Purpose-built flow and jump trails from town; all levels
destinations.pitch: Hundreds of kilometres of purpose-built trails start from downtown, funded by the Walton family. It's become the 'mountain bike capital of the world' in America's least likely state.

children.name: Slaughter Pen
children.note: The original network: jump lines and flow, right from town

children.name: Coler Mountain Bike Preserve
children.note: Downhill-style lines, drops and a bike-in café

children.name: Back 40 (Bella Vista)
children.note: ~50 km loop of rocky, rooty singletrack

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops, with trail, gravel and e-bikes

destinations.name: Fruita
destinations.terrain: Desert ridgelines and buff singletrack; beginner to advanced
destinations.pitch: A small desert town with two big networks: the fast ridge-top trails of 18 Road and the river-canyon loops of Kokopelli. Laid-back and cheaper than Moab, 2 hours away.

children.name: 18 Road (Bookcliffs)
children.note: Fast, flowy ridgelines like Zippity Do Da

children.name: Kokopelli Loops (Mary's Loop)
children.note: Canyon-rim tech above the Colorado River

destinations.hireNote: A few good shops in town renting trail bikes

destinations.name: Crested Butte
destinations.terrain: High-alpine singletrack through aspen and wildflowers; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: One of the birthplaces of mountain biking, with high alpine singletrack like the 401 Trail through summer wildflowers, plus a lift-served bike park.
destinations.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms are common in July and August: start early.

children.name: 401 Trail
children.note: ~25 km loop topping out ~3,500 m; wildflowers in July

children.name: Evolution Bike Park
children.note: Lift-served park on Mt Crested Butte

destinations.hireNote: Shops in town and at the resort bike park

destinations.name: East Burke (Kingdom Trails)
destinations.terrain: Flowy, rooty New England singletrack on private land; all levels
destinations.pitch: A huge network across farmland and forest around East Burke, built through agreements with dozens of private landowners. Autumn colours make late September special.

children.name: Darling Hill
children.note: The classic flow trails (Kitchel, Sidewinder)

children.name: Burke Mountain Bike Park
children.note: Lift-served downhill above the village

destinations.hireNote: East Burke Sports and the Kingdom Trails shop rent bikes by the trails; book ahead in summer

destinations.name: Bend
destinations.terrain: Fast volcanic singletrack through pine forest; beginner to advanced
destinations.pitch: A sunny high-desert town with smooth, fast trails starting at the edge of town, from Phil's Trail network to the high-country lines on Mt Bachelor.

children.name: Phil's Trail network
children.note: Dozens of linked loops 10 minutes from downtown

children.name: Tumalo Creek & Mrazek
children.note: Longer, higher, with waterfalls and big descents

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops renting trail and gravel bikes

destinations.name: Brevard (Pisgah)
destinations.terrain: Rocky, rooty, steep Appalachian singletrack; advanced
destinations.pitch: Old-school, technical riding in the Pisgah National Forest: long climbs, loose rock and roots, and some of the toughest trails in the East.

children.name: Pisgah Ranger District trails
children.note: Black Mountain, Farlow Gap: long and gnarly

children.name: DuPont State Forest
children.note: Smoother slickrock and waterfalls; friendlier

destinations.hireNote: A few shops in Brevard; book ahead

destinations.name: Finale Ligure
destinations.terrain: Rocky, loose enduro trails from the hills to the sea; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Enduro trails that end at the beach, with shuttles running all day and a riding season that lasts all winter. The old Enduro World Series finale made it famous.
destinations.weather: Rides all year; July and August are hot and busy.

children.name: Feglino & Base NATO area
children.note: Shuttle-served descents: Roller Coaster, DH Kill

children.name: Varigotti & Perti
children.note: Coastal lines with sea views

destinations.hireNote: Dozens of shops and shuttle companies with high-end bikes and e-bikes

destinations.name: Morzine (Portes du Soleil)
destinations.terrain: Lift-served bike parks and big-mountain singletrack; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: A dozen linked bike parks across France and Switzerland on one pass, with famously rough, braking-bump-ridden downhill tracks and a huge summer scene.

children.name: Pleney (Morzine)
children.note: Steep, rough classic downhill trails

children.name: Les Gets Bike Park
children.note: Flow, jumps and a former World Cup track

children.name: Châtel Bike Park
children.note: Big jump lines and slopestyle features

children.name: Champéry (Switzerland)
children.note: Swiss side: steep World Cup downhill

destinations.hireNote: Many shops renting downhill, enduro and e-bikes

destinations.name: Lenzerheide
destinations.terrain: Bike kingdom of flow trails, World Cup tracks and alpine singletrack; all levels
destinations.pitch: A Swiss resort that rebuilt itself around biking, with flow trails, a World Cup downhill track and long alpine rides with lifts and trains for the uphill.

children.name: Bike Kingdom (Rothorn)
children.note: Flow lines, jump trails and the World Cup track

destinations.hireNote: Bike-park, trail and e-bikes for hire in the village

destinations.name: Saalbach-Leogang
destinations.terrain: Lift-served flow and freeride lines across two valleys; all levels
destinations.pitch: Austria's biggest bike area: many lifts, long flow trails and a regular World Cup downhill venue at Leogang.

children.name: Bikepark Leogang
children.note: World Cup downhill, jump lines and a pump track

children.name: Saalbach Hacklberg & Z-Line
children.note: Long flow and freeride lines

destinations.hireNote: Bike-park, trail and e-bikes for hire in every village

destinations.name: Riva del Garda (Lake Garda)
destinations.terrain: Rocky old military tracks and singletrack above the lake; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Big climbs on old military roads, rocky descents and a lakeside town with gelato at the end. Monte Altissimo and Tremalzo are the classics.

children.name: Tremalzo
children.note: Old military road with tunnels and hairpins; huge views

children.name: Monte Altissimo
children.note: ~2,000 m climb, long rocky descent to the lake

destinations.hireNote: Many shops in Riva and Torbole, with mountain, road and e-bikes

destinations.name: Madeira
destinations.terrain: Steep enduro trails from mountains to sea, with shuttles; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Volcanic island enduro with shuttles, rides from the clouds to the ocean through laurel forest, and mild weather all year.
destinations.weather: Mild year-round; the north side and high ground are often in cloud.

children.name: Paul da Serra plateau
children.note: High moorland starts, long descents

destinations.hireNote: Several operators rent enduro and e-bikes, often with shuttle tours

destinations.name: Peebles (Tweed Valley)
destinations.terrain: Forest trail centres, enduro and steep natural tracks; all levels
destinations.pitch: Scotland's riding heartland, with the Glentress trail centre, the steep tracks of Innerleithen and the Golfie, and the Enduro World Series has raced here.
destinations.weather: Rides all year, but it's often wet: summer is the most reliable.

children.name: Glentress
children.note: Waymarked trail centre: blue to black, plus skills park

children.name: Innerleithen & the Golfie
children.note: Steep downhill and enduro tracks with uplift days

destinations.hireNote: A couple of shops at Glentress and in Peebles

destinations.name: Aínsa (Zona Zero)
destinations.terrain: Over 1,000 km of waymarked trails, rocky and natural; all levels
destinations.pitch: A medieval hilltop village in the Spanish Pyrenees surrounded by one of Europe's biggest waymarked trail networks. Quiet, cheap and technical.

children.name: Zona Zero network
children.note: Waymarked enduro and XC routes around Aínsa and Boltaña

destinations.hireNote: Mostly through guiding and shuttle outfits; more shops further east in Benasque and Castejón de Sos

destinations.name: Rotorua
destinations.terrain: Loamy flow trails in redwood forest, plus a gondola bike park; all levels
destinations.pitch: Flowing trails through giant redwoods and pine, starting at the edge of town, with geothermal pools for afterwards. Whakarewarewa Forest is the heart.

children.name: Whakarewarewa Forest
children.note: ~200 km of graded trails among the redwoods

children.name: Skyline Rotorua
children.note: Gondola-served flow and jump trails

destinations.hireNote: Several shops right by the Whakarewarewa forest

destinations.name: Queenstown
destinations.terrain: Gondola bike park, alpine singletrack and heli drops; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: A gondola straight from town to a big bike park, alpine trails at Coronet Peak and Cardrona, and heli-biking into the high country.

children.name: Queenstown Bike Park (Skyline)
children.note: Gondola-served, ~30 trails

children.name: Coronet Peak & Cardrona
children.note: Alpine bike parks over summer

children.name: Seven Mile
children.note: Forest singletrack on the lake road

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops, with bike-park, trail and e-bikes

destinations.name: Derby (Blue Derby)
destinations.terrain: Purpose-built flow and tech trails through rainforest; all levels
destinations.pitch: An old tin-mining town in northeast Tasmania revived by the Blue Derby trails: rainforest, granite and creek crossings, with shuttles to the top of the network.

children.name: Blue Tier
children.note: Big descent from the alpine plateau; shuttle up

children.name: Derby core network
children.note: Linked loops right from the village

destinations.hireNote: Several shops and shuttle companies in this small town

destinations.name: Stellenbosch
destinations.terrain: Singletrack through vineyards and fynbos mountains; all levels
destinations.pitch: Trails among vineyards and mountains half an hour from Cape Town, from Jonkershoek's steep enduro to the Cape Epic stage routes.
destinations.weather: Winter (June–August) is the rainy season in the Cape.

children.name: Jonkershoek
children.note: Steep mountain trails in a nature reserve

children.name: Tokai & Table Mountain
children.note: Forest trails on Cape Town's doorstep

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops, including a Specialized centre with a full rental fleet

destinations.name: Upper Mustang
destinations.airport: Pokhara, then flight or jeep to Jomsom
destinations.terrain: Jeep tracks and singletrack in high desert; strong intermediate
destinations.pitch: A ride through the former Kingdom of Lo, a Tibetan-Buddhist high desert in Nepal's rain shadow, from Jomsom to the walled town of Lo Manthang.
destinations.weather: Lies in the Himalayan rain shadow, so it's rideable even in the monsoon (June–August).
destinations.hireNote: Bikes hired in Pokhara or Kathmandu are basic; most riders bring their own or go with a tour operator

destinations.name: Colorado Trail
destinations.terrain: High-altitude singletrack with big hike-a-bike sections; advanced
destinations.pitch: Around 800 km of mostly singletrack from Denver to Durango, much of it above 3,000 m. Bikes detour around six wilderness areas.
destinations.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms near-daily in July; the high passes can hold snow into early July.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for bikepacking, with bags and a light load

destinations.name: Kokopelli Trail
destinations.terrain: Desert jeep roads and some singletrack; intermediate, but remote
destinations.pitch: A classic desert bikepacking route from Fruita to Moab, through canyons and over the La Sal foothills, linking two mountain-bike towns.
destinations.hireNote: Bikes can be hired in Fruita or Moab, but most riders bring their own

destinations.name: Girona
destinations.terrain: Quiet backroads, classic climbs and coast roads; also the gravel capital of Europe
destinations.pitch: Europe's pro-cyclist hometown: smooth, quiet roads, famous training climbs like Rocacorba and Els Àngels, coffee shops full of riders, and endless gravel.

children.name: Rocacorba
children.note: ~10 km at ~6.5%, steeper near the top; the pros' test climb

children.name: Els Àngels
children.note: ~10 km steady climb to a hilltop sanctuary

children.name: Sant Feliu de Guíxols coast road
children.note: Twisty cliff road along the Costa Brava

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of high-end road and gravel bikes

destinations.name: Mallorca
destinations.terrain: Mountain roads in the Serra de Tramuntana and flat island lanes; all levels
destinations.pitch: The classic spring training island: the Sa Calobra hairpins, the Puig Major climb and quiet lanes across the plains, with mild weather when the north is cold.

children.name: Sa Calobra
children.note: ~9.5 km at ~7%: a famous loop of hairpins down to the sea (and back up)

children.name: Puig Major
children.note: ~14 km to ~880 m, the island's longest climb

children.name: Cap de Formentor
children.note: Cliff road to a lighthouse at the northern tip

destinations.hireNote: Hundreds of road bikes for hire across the island

destinations.name: Tenerife (Teide)
destinations.terrain: Long climbs from sea level to over 2,000 m; mostly advanced
destinations.pitch: A volcano you can climb from the beach: roads rise from sea level to over 2,000 m in the Teide National Park, where pro teams base winter altitude camps.

children.name: Teide from Los Cristianos
children.note: ~40 km climb from the coast into the caldera

destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting good road bikes

destinations.name: Calpe & the Costa Blanca
destinations.terrain: Quiet mountain roads behind the coast; all levels
destinations.pitch: The winter base of the pro peloton: mild sunny weather, empty inland mountain roads and climbs like the Coll de Rates.

children.name: Coll de Rates
children.note: ~6.5 km steady climb, the classic local test

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops renting high-end road bikes

destinations.name: Corvara (Dolomites passes)
destinations.terrain: High mountain passes with hairpins; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: The Giro d'Italia's favourite playground: the Sella Ronda loop over four passes around the Sella group, the steep Giau and the Fedaia under the Marmolada glacier.

children.name: Sella Ronda (Pordoi, Sella, Gardena, Campolongo)
children.note: ~55 km loop over four passes; car-free days some summers

children.name: Passo Giau
children.note: ~10 km at ~9% from Selva, 29 hairpins

children.name: Passo Fedaia
children.note: Steep ramps under the Marmolada glacier

destinations.hireNote: Road and e-bikes for hire in most valley towns

destinations.name: Bormio (Stelvio & Gavia)
destinations.terrain: Giant alpine climbs; advanced
destinations.pitch: Some of the hardest and most famous climbs in cycling, all within reach of Bormio: the Stelvio, the Gavia and the brutal Mortirolo.
destinations.weather: High passes usually open late May or June and can close with early snow in October.

children.name: Passo dello Stelvio
children.note: ~22 km at ~7% from Bormio to 2,757 m; 48 hairpins on the Prato side

children.name: Passo Gavia
children.note: ~26 km to 2,621 m, narrow and wild

children.name: Mortirolo
children.note: ~12 km at ~10.5% from Mazzo; brutally steep

destinations.hireNote: Several shops in Bormio renting road and e-bikes

destinations.name: Bourg d'Oisans (Alpe d'Huez)
destinations.terrain: Tour de France climbs; advanced
destinations.pitch: Bourg d'Oisans sits at the foot of the most famous Tour de France climbs: the 21 hairpins of Alpe d'Huez, the Galibier and the Croix de Fer.

children.name: Alpe d'Huez
children.note: ~13.8 km at ~8%, 21 numbered hairpins

children.name: Col du Galibier
children.note: ~18 km from Valloire to 2,642 m (via the Télégraphe)

children.name: Col de la Croix de Fer
children.note: ~30 km of varied climbing to 2,067 m

destinations.hireNote: Several shops in Bourg d'Oisans renting road bikes

destinations.name: Bédoin (Mont Ventoux)
destinations.terrain: One giant climb with three routes up; advanced
destinations.pitch: The 'Giant of Provence': a bare, windswept limestone summit at 1,910 m, climbed from three sides. Some riders do all three in a day.
destinations.weather: The summit road usually closes to cars in winter, and the mistral wind can be fierce.

children.name: From Bédoin
children.note: ~21 km at ~7.5%; the Tour route, through forest then the bare moonscape

children.name: From Malaucène
children.note: ~21 km, steeper in places

children.name: From Sault
children.note: ~26 km, the gentlest way up

destinations.hireNote: Shops in Bédoin and Malaucène rent road and e-bikes

destinations.name: Luz-Saint-Sauveur (Tourmalet)
destinations.terrain: Tour de France climbs; advanced
destinations.pitch: The Tourmalet, the most-climbed pass in Tour de France history, plus the Aubisque, Aspin, Peyresourde and Hautacam, all within a day's ride of each other.

children.name: Col du Tourmalet
children.note: ~19 km at ~7.4% from Luz-Saint-Sauveur to 2,115 m

children.name: Col d'Aubisque
children.note: ~16.5 km from Laruns, then the cliffside road to the Soulor

children.name: Hautacam
children.note: ~13.5 km summit finish above Argelès

children.name: Peyresourde & Aspin
children.note: Shorter, steady classic cols

destinations.hireNote: A few shops in Luz rent carbon road bikes and e-bikes; book ahead in summer

destinations.name: Oudenaarde (Flanders)
destinations.terrain: Short, steep cobbled climbs and farm lanes; all levels (the cobbles hurt)
destinations.pitch: The home of the Tour of Flanders: short, brutal cobbled climbs like the Oude Kwaremont and Paterberg, a museum, and a country obsessed with bike racing.
destinations.weather: Spring classics season is March–April, when it's often cold and wet.

children.name: Oude Kwaremont
children.note: ~2.2 km of cobbles, the race's longest

children.name: Paterberg
children.note: ~360 m of cobbles up to ~20%

children.name: Koppenberg
children.note: ~600 m of rough cobbles up to ~22%

children.name: Muur van Geraardsbergen
children.note: Cobbled wall to a chapel; up to ~20%

destinations.hireNote: Good road bikes at the Tour of Flanders Centre and a couple of other shops

destinations.name: Roubaix (Paris–Roubaix cobbles)
destinations.terrain: Flat, very rough cobbled farm tracks; all levels, hard on bikes
destinations.pitch: Ride the 'Hell of the North' on the same cobbled sectors as the race, including the Arenberg Forest, and finish with a lap of the Roubaix velodrome.

children.name: Trouée d'Arenberg
children.note: ~2.3 km straight cobbled track through the forest

children.name: Carrefour de l'Arbre
children.note: Five-star sector near the finish

children.name: Roubaix velodrome
children.note: The finish; showers with riders' name plaques

destinations.hireNote: Hire is mostly set up for the Paris–Roubaix Challenge weekend; otherwise most riders bring their own

destinations.name: Bellagio (Lake Como)
destinations.terrain: Lakeside roads and steep climbs; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: Lakeside roads, climbs from the Giro di Lombardia, and the Madonna del Ghisallo chapel, the patron saint of cyclists, with a cycling museum beside it.

children.name: Madonna del Ghisallo
children.note: ~10 km from Bellagio to the cyclists' chapel

children.name: Muro di Sormano
children.note: ~2 km at ~15%, with gradients painted on the road

destinations.hireNote: Road and e-bikes for hire around the lake

destinations.name: Andermatt (Swiss passes)
destinations.terrain: Big alpine passes; advanced
destinations.pitch: Andermatt sits at the centre of a ring of famous passes: the Furka, Grimsel, Susten and the cobbled Tremola road on the Gotthard.

children.name: Furka Pass
children.note: To 2,429 m, past the Rhône Glacier

children.name: Grimsel Pass
children.note: To 2,164 m between reservoirs

children.name: Susten Pass
children.note: To 2,224 m, glacier views

children.name: Gotthard (Tremola)
children.note: Historic cobbled hairpins to 2,106 m

destinations.hireNote: A BMC test centre in Andermatt rents premium road bikes; a few other shops too

destinations.name: Oviedo (Angliru & Covadonga)
destinations.terrain: Brutally steep Vuelta climbs; advanced
destinations.pitch: Green mountains with some of the steepest climbs in pro cycling: the Angliru, with ramps over 20%, and the Lagos de Covadonga in the Picos de Europa.
destinations.weather: Atlantic climate: green because it rains a lot, even in summer.

children.name: Alto de l'Angliru
children.note: ~12.5 km at ~10%, ramps up to ~23%

children.name: Lagos de Covadonga
children.note: ~12.5 km at ~7% to mountain lakes

destinations.hireNote: A few shops in Oviedo; a car helps to reach the climbs

destinations.name: Hualien (Taroko & Wuling)
destinations.airport: Taipei ~2.5 h by train to Hualien
destinations.terrain: One very long climb from the sea to 3,275 m; advanced
destinations.pitch: One of the longest paved climbs in the world: from the Pacific coast through Taroko Gorge to Wuling Pass at 3,275 m, about 100 km of almost non-stop climbing.
destinations.weather: Avoid typhoon season (July–September); winter can bring frost and snow at the top.

children.name: Wuling Pass
children.note: 3,275 m, Taiwan's highest road

destinations.hireNote: Giant by Hualien station rents road bikes; book ahead and check sizes

destinations.name: Boulder
destinations.terrain: Canyon climbs and high plains; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: An American pro-cycling hub at the foot of the Rockies: canyon climbs, Flagstaff Mountain from town, and Trail Ridge Road in Rocky Mountain National Park.

children.name: Flagstaff Mountain
children.note: ~7 km from town, steep at the top

children.name: Lefthand Canyon to Ward
children.note: ~25 km steady canyon climb

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops renting road and gravel bikes

destinations.name: Pāʻia (Haleakalā)
destinations.terrain: One very long climb from sea level to over 3,000 m; advanced
destinations.pitch: Climb from sea level at Pā'ia to the summit of a volcano at 3,055 m: one of the biggest elevation gains of any paved road on earth.

children.name: Haleakalā summit
children.note: ~57 km, ~3,000 m of gain

destinations.hireNote: Road-bike hire is scarce; Pāʻia shops mostly rent mountain bikes for the downhill tours

destinations.name: Danube Cycle Path (Passau–Vienna)
destinations.airport: Munich ~2 h to Passau; Vienna airport at the end
destinations.terrain: Flat, paved riverside path; easy
destinations.pitch: Europe's most popular long-distance bike path, the Austrian part of EuroVelo 6: flat riverside riding through the Wachau's vineyards and monasteries to Vienna.

children.name: Wachau valley
children.note: Vineyards, Melk Abbey and apricot orchards

destinations.hireNote: One-way hire along the route, including e-bikes

destinations.name: Loire à Vélo
destinations.airport: Paris ~1 h by train to the middle of the route
destinations.terrain: Flat, waymarked lanes and paths; easy
destinations.pitch: A waymarked route along the Loire to the Atlantic, part of EuroVelo 6, past Renaissance châteaux and vineyards. Easy riding with wine at the end of each day.

children.name: Châteaux stretch (Blois–Tours)
children.note: Chambord, Chenonceau and Amboise within reach

destinations.hireNote: One-way hire along the route, including e-bikes

destinations.name: Route des Grandes Alpes
destinations.region: Alps, Lake Geneva to the Mediterranean
destinations.terrain: Big alpine passes, day after day; advanced
destinations.pitch: A classic road through the French Alps from Lake Geneva to the Mediterranean, over passes like the Iseran, Galibier and Izoard.

children.name: Col de l'Iseran
children.note: 2,764 m, the highest paved pass in the Alps

children.name: Col d'Izoard
children.note: Through the eerie 'Casse Déserte'

destinations.hireNote: No one-way hire: rent near the start and arrange the return, or go with a tour company

destinations.name: Shimanami Kaido
destinations.terrain: Dedicated bike lanes over bridges and islands; easy
destinations.pitch: A car-free route of bridges and bike lanes hopping across six islands of the Seto Inland Sea, with citrus groves, temples and rental bikes at both ends.
destinations.weather: June is the rainy season and typhoons can hit in late summer.
destinations.hireNote: One-way hire at either end and at stations along the way, including e-bikes

destinations.name: Lhasa to Kathmandu
destinations.airport: Fly or take the train to Lhasa
destinations.terrain: Mostly paved high-altitude road over passes above 5,000 m; advanced, very high
destinations.pitch: Across the Tibetan Plateau past Everest views and over passes above 5,000 m, then a huge descent into Nepal. Foreigners can only travel in Tibet on an organised tour.
destinations.weather: Permits and border status change: check current access.
destinations.hireNote: Most riders go with a tour operator, which may hire bikes; otherwise bring your own

destinations.name: Siena (Tuscany)
destinations.terrain: White gravel roads through vineyards and hills; all levels
destinations.pitch: The white gravel roads of Chianti and the Crete Senesi, home to the L'Eroica vintage ride and the Strade Bianche race, with Siena's Piazza del Campo at the end.

children.name: L'Eroica routes (Gaiole)
children.note: Waymarked routes on the old white roads

children.name: Crete Senesi
children.note: Rolling clay hills and cypress avenues

destinations.hireNote: Road, gravel and e-bikes for hire in Siena and the Chianti towns

destinations.name: Emporia (Flint Hills)
destinations.terrain: Rough, rocky prairie gravel; long and exposed
destinations.pitch: The tallgrass prairie of the Flint Hills is home to Unbound Gravel, the biggest race in gravel, held each spring on sharp flint roads around Emporia.
destinations.hireNote: A couple of shops in Emporia rent bikes; call ahead, especially around Unbound

destinations.name: Steamboat Springs
destinations.terrain: Smooth ranch roads and mountain gravel; all levels
destinations.pitch: Ranch-country gravel in the Yampa Valley, with SBT GRVL each summer and hot springs after the ride.
destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting gravel and mountain bikes

destinations.name: Aviemore (Cairngorms)
destinations.terrain: Estate tracks and forest roads through the national park; all levels
destinations.pitch: Old Caledonian pine forest, estate tracks and empty glens in Britain's biggest national park, with whisky distilleries along the Spey.
destinations.weather: Midges in summer; weather can be wintry on the hills any month.

children.name: Rothiemurchus & Glenmore
children.note: Forest tracks around Loch Morlich

destinations.hireNote: A couple of shops in Aviemore

destinations.name: Iceland Highlands (Kjölur)
destinations.terrain: Rough volcanic gravel roads (F-roads) and river crossings; intermediate, remote
destinations.pitch: A crossing of Iceland's empty interior between glaciers on the old Kjölur route, with hot springs at Hveravellir halfway.
destinations.weather: Highland roads usually open in late June or July; wind is the main challenge.
destinations.hireNote: Hire in Reykjavík is limited and basic; most riders bring their own

destinations.name: Carretera Austral
destinations.terrain: Mixed paved and rough gravel road; intermediate, long
destinations.pitch: A road carved through Chilean Patagonia past fjords, glaciers and temperate rainforest, ending at Villa O'Higgins. One of the world's great bike tours.
destinations.weather: Rain is frequent, and the wind can be relentless.
destinations.hireNote: Hire is rare; most riders bring their own

destinations.name: Pamir Highway
destinations.terrain: Broken tarmac and gravel at very high altitude; advanced, remote
destinations.pitch: The 'Roof of the World' road through Tajikistan's Pamirs, along the Afghan border on the Panj River, then over the Ak-Baital Pass at 4,655 m.
destinations.weather: Needs a special GBAO permit. Check travel advisories before planning.
destinations.hireNote: Spares are hard to find on the way, so carry what you need

destinations.name: Great Divide Route
destinations.terrain: Forest roads and backroads along the Continental Divide; long and remote
destinations.pitch: The classic North American bikepacking route along the Rocky Mountains from Banff to the Mexican border, and the course of the Tour Divide race.
destinations.weather: Snow lingers on northern passes into June; grizzly country in Canada and Montana.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for bikepacking; shops along the way can help with repairs

destinations.name: Atlas Mountains
destinations.terrain: Mountain pistes, mule tracks and desert roads; advanced, remote
destinations.pitch: Mountain pistes across the High and Anti-Atlas from Marrakech, the route of the Atlas Mountain Race, past Berber villages and kasbahs.
destinations.hireNote: Tour operators in Marrakech hire bikes; otherwise bring your own

destinations.name: Alps 2 Ocean
destinations.airport: Christchurch ~4 h to the start; Queenstown ~2.5 h
destinations.terrain: Purpose-built gravel trail and quiet roads; easy to intermediate
destinations.pitch: From the foot of Aoraki/Mount Cook past glacier lakes and hydro dams down to Oamaru on the Pacific coast: New Zealand's longest single cycle trail.
destinations.hireNote: Trail operators hire bikes and e-bikes, with luggage transfers and shuttles

destinations.name: Jordan Bike Trail
destinations.terrain: Desert tracks, village roads and singletrack; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: A route the length of Jordan, through olive hills and canyons to Petra and the red sand of Wadi Rum, finishing at the Red Sea.
destinations.weather: Summer is far too hot; winter can bring rain and snow on the high plateau.
destinations.hireNote: Hire mainly through tour operators; self-supported riders bring their own

destinations.name: Baja Divide
destinations.airport: San Diego (start), San José del Cabo (end)
destinations.terrain: Sandy desert tracks and dirt roads; advanced, very remote
destinations.pitch: A self-supported dirt route down the Baja peninsula through cactus deserts, missions and fishing villages, between the Pacific and the Sea of Cortez.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for sand and long dry stretches

destinations.name: Congo Nile Trail
destinations.terrain: Dirt roads along the lake with constant climbing; intermediate
destinations.pitch: Dirt roads along the shore of Lake Kivu through tea and coffee plantations and villages, in the 'land of a thousand hills'.
destinations.weather: Dry seasons are June–September and December–February.
destinations.hireNote: A couple of outfits in Rubavu and Kigali hire mountain bikes

destinations.name: Park City
destinations.terrain: Smooth, buff singletrack through aspen, plus lift-served flow and downhill; all levels
destinations.pitch: Hundreds of kilometres of smooth singletrack climb through aspen and pine right from town, with lift-served riding at Deer Valley and Park City Mountain and the Wasatch Crest ridge above it all.
destinations.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms are common in July and August.

children.name: Wasatch Crest Trail
children.note: Ridge-top classic at ~3,000 m from Guardsman Pass, usually shuttled; snow-free ~July–October

children.name: Deer Valley Bike Park
children.note: Lift-served downhill and flow trails

children.name: Park City Mountain
children.note: Summer lifts from Canyons Village, and the long Mid Mountain trail across the resort

children.name: Round Valley
children.note: Rolling sagebrush trails at the edge of town; the first to dry out in spring

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops renting trail, downhill and e-bikes

destinations.name: St George
destinations.airport: St George ~15 min; Las Vegas ~2 h
destinations.terrain: Slickrock, lava ledges and fast desert singletrack; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Utah's winter riding: red-rock and lava-ledge trails around St George and Hurricane, from the slickrock of Gooseberry Mesa to fast desert singletrack, with Zion National Park next door.
destinations.weather: Summer is very hot, often above 38°C.

children.name: Gooseberry Mesa
children.note: Slickrock and ledges on a mesa top with views to Zion; technical

children.name: Hurricane Cliffs (JEM)
children.note: Fast, flowing desert singletrack along the cliffs; a good first day

children.name: Zen Trail
children.note: Steep, ledgy slickrock right above town; expert

children.name: Bearclaw Poppy
children.note: Rolling, pumpy desert trail; beginner–intermediate

destinations.hireNote: Several shops in St George and Hurricane rent trail bikes

destinations.name: Brian Head
destinations.airport: Cedar City ~45 min; Las Vegas ~3 h
destinations.terrain: Lift-served flow and downhill plus high-alpine singletrack; all levels
destinations.pitch: Utah's highest resort, at almost 3,000 m: a lift-served bike park, alpine singletrack among red cliffs, and long shuttled descents off the plateau. Cool when the desert below is baking.

children.name: Brian Head Bike Park
children.note: Lift-served flow and downhill

children.name: Dark Hollow to Parowan
children.note: Long shuttled descent off the plateau; intermediate–advanced

children.name: Thunder Mountain (Red Canyon)
children.note: ~1 h east: singletrack through red hoodoos near Bryce Canyon

destinations.hireNote: The resort rents bike-park bikes; more choice in Cedar City

destinations.name: Salt Lake City
destinations.terrain: Foothill and canyon singletrack, plus long road climbs; all levels
destinations.pitch: A city with mountains at the end of the street: the Bonneville Shoreline Trail along the foothills, the purpose-built Corner Canyon network to the south, and long road climbs up the Cottonwood canyons to the ski resorts.
destinations.weather: Summer is hot in the valley; ride early, or head up the canyons.

children.name: Corner Canyon
children.note: Big purpose-built network in Draper, ~30 min south; flow and tech

children.name: Bonneville Shoreline Trail
children.note: Foothill singletrack along an ancient lakeshore above the city

children.name: Sundance Bike Park
children.note: ~1 h south: lift-served trails in Provo Canyon

children.name: Little Cottonwood Canyon
children.note: ~13 km at ~8% to Snowbird and Alta

children.name: Big Cottonwood Canyon
children.note: ~24 km, ~1,150 m to Brighton; steadier

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops renting trail, road and e-bikes

destinations.name: White Rim Road
destinations.terrain: Jeep road over sand and rock; not technical, but long, hot and remote
destinations.pitch: A loop below the cliffs of Canyonlands' Island in the Sky, on a jeep road along a white sandstone bench above the Green and Colorado rivers. Camping is by permit, and most groups bring a support vehicle to carry the water.
destinations.weather: Campsite permits for spring and autumn are booked months ahead; there's no water on the route.
destinations.hireNote: Moab shops rent bikes, and outfitters run supported trips

destinations.name: North Vancouver (North Shore)
destinations.terrain: Steep, rooty, rocky forest trails and wooden features; advanced
destinations.pitch: The birthplace of freeride: steep, rooty rainforest trails on Fromme, Seymour and Cypress, famous for their wooden features, ten minutes from downtown Vancouver.
destinations.weather: Wet from October to April, when the roots and rock get very slippery.

children.name: Mount Fromme
children.note: Steep, technical classics; climb the road to the top

children.name: Mount Seymour
children.note: Slightly friendlier, with a few flow trails

children.name: Cypress
children.note: Raw, steep and rough; for experts

destinations.hireNote: Several shops near the trails rent high-end bikes

destinations.name: Kamloops (& Sun Peaks)
destinations.terrain: Dry, steep desert trails and a lift-served bike park; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Dry, dusty hillside trails above town that ride when the coast is wet, the free Kamloops Bike Ranch, and Sun Peaks' lift-served bike park up the road.
destinations.weather: July and August are hot in town; ride Sun Peaks then.

children.name: Kamloops Bike Ranch
children.note: Free park with dirt jumps, flow and downhill lines

children.name: Sun Peaks Bike Park
children.note: ~45 min: lift-served downhill and flow

destinations.hireNote: Shops in town, and bike-park rentals at Sun Peaks

destinations.name: Mont-Sainte-Anne
destinations.terrain: Rocky, rooty World Cup downhill and a big cross-country network; all levels
destinations.pitch: A long-time World Cup venue near Quebec City: gondola-served downhill on rocky, rooty eastern terrain and a big cross-country network, with the St Lawrence below.
destinations.weather: Rain makes the roots and rock very slick.

children.name: Mont-Sainte-Anne Bike Park
children.note: Gondola-served downhill, including the World Cup track

children.name: Cross-country trails
children.note: A big network of rooty forest singletrack

destinations.hireNote: Downhill and trail bikes for hire at the resort

destinations.name: Durango
destinations.terrain: Rocky singletrack from town and high-alpine trails above; all levels
destinations.pitch: A mountain-bike town since it hosted the first world championships in 1990, with trails right from Main Street, alpine singletrack in the San Juans, lift-served riding at Purgatory and big road passes to the north.
destinations.weather: Afternoon storms in July and August; high trails are snow-free from about July.

children.name: Horse Gulch
children.note: Rocky, fun town trails minutes from downtown

children.name: Colorado Trail (Kennebec)
children.note: High-alpine classic at ~3,500 m; usually shuttled

children.name: Purgatory Bike Park
children.note: ~40 min north: lift-served downhill and flow

children.name: Coal Bank & Molas passes
children.note: Two big passes on the road to Silverton

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops renting trail, road and e-bikes

destinations.name: Ketchum (Sun Valley)
destinations.terrain: Long, smooth singletrack and lift-served descents; all levels
destinations.pitch: Hundreds of kilometres of smooth singletrack through sagebrush and aspen, and gondola-served descents off Bald Mountain, in a quiet mountain valley.

children.name: Bald Mountain
children.note: Gondola-served flow and long descents

children.name: Adams Gulch
children.note: Classic loops just north of town

destinations.hireNote: Several shops in Ketchum rent trail and e-bikes

destinations.name: Mammoth Lakes
destinations.airport: Mammoth Yosemite ~15 min; Los Angeles ~5 h
destinations.terrain: Volcanic pumice trails and lift-served downhill; all levels
destinations.pitch: A big lift-served bike park on the pumice slopes of an old volcano, plus high-Sierra singletrack between alpine lakes.
destinations.weather: Afternoon storms in summer, and the altitude takes a day or two to get used to.

children.name: Mammoth Bike Park
children.note: Gondola to the 3,370 m summit, with long pumice descents

children.name: Lakes Basin
children.note: Cross-country loops among alpine lakes

destinations.hireNote: Bike-park and trail bikes for hire at the resort and in town

destinations.name: Downieville
destinations.terrain: Long, rocky shuttled descents; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: A Gold Rush town with a famous shuttle ride: the Downieville Downhill drops from Packer Saddle back to town, and it ends with a swim in the Yuba River.
destinations.weather: The canyon is hot in midsummer; ride early.

children.name: Downieville Downhill
children.note: ~24 km, ~1,300 m of descent from Packer Saddle; shuttled

destinations.hireNote: The shuttle companies in town rent a small fleet; book ahead

destinations.name: Truckee (Lake Tahoe)
destinations.terrain: Granite singletrack, lake views and lift-served parks; all levels
destinations.pitch: Granite and pine around the lake: the Flume Trail high above the water, Northstar's lift-served bike park, and the classic road loop around Lake Tahoe.

children.name: Flume Trail
children.note: Cliffside trail high above the east shore; usually shuttled

children.name: Northstar Bike Park
children.note: Lift-served downhill and flow

destinations.hireNote: Shops around the lake rent trail, road and e-bikes

destinations.name: Bellingham
destinations.terrain: Rooty, loamy forest singletrack, from flow to steep tech; all levels
destinations.pitch: Galbraith Mountain, on the edge of town, has around 100 km of community-built forest trails, from jump lines to steep, rooty tech, with coastal riding at Chuckanut too.
destinations.weather: Wet from October to April; the trails ride all year but get muddy.

children.name: Galbraith Mountain
children.note: Around 100 km of trails on the edge of town

children.name: Chuckanut
children.note: Coastal trails with sea views; rougher and steeper

destinations.hireNote: A few shops rent trail bikes; book ahead

destinations.name: Copper Harbor
destinations.terrain: Rocky, rooty northwoods singletrack and big built flow lines; all levels
destinations.pitch: A tiny town at the tip of the Keweenaw Peninsula on Lake Superior, with rocky northwoods trails and long, built descents with big berms and jumps.
destinations.weather: Snow lingers into May, and black flies are bad in June.

children.name: Flow Motion & Overflow
children.note: Long built descents off Brockway Mountain

children.name: Brockway Mountain
children.note: Rock and big views over Lake Superior

destinations.hireNote: A couple of shops in town rent bikes

destinations.name: Tucson
destinations.terrain: Desert roads with wide shoulders, and one huge climb; all levels
destinations.pitch: A winter base for pros and amateurs: dry, warm days, bike-friendly roads and the climb up Mount Lemmon, from saguaro cactus to pine forest.
destinations.weather: Summer is extremely hot; ride at dawn if at all.

children.name: Mount Lemmon
children.note: ~40 km, ~1,800 m from the desert floor to Summerhaven

children.name: Gates Pass
children.note: Short, steep pass west of town among saguaros

destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting good road bikes

destinations.name: Santa Barbara
destinations.airport: Santa Barbara ~15 min; Los Angeles ~2 h
destinations.terrain: Coastal roads and steep mountain climbs; all levels
destinations.pitch: Pros winter here for the mild weather and the steep climbs behind the city, with flat coast roads and the Santa Ynez Valley wine country over the hill.
destinations.weather: The coast is often foggy in early summer.

children.name: Gibraltar Road
children.note: ~10 km, steep, above the city and the sea

children.name: Figueroa Mountain
children.note: Steep climb above the Santa Ynez Valley, near Solvang

destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting road and e-bikes

destinations.name: Healdsburg (Sonoma)
destinations.airport: Santa Rosa ~15 min; San Francisco ~1.5 h
destinations.terrain: Quiet vineyard roads, steep coastal climbs and dirt fire roads; all levels
destinations.pitch: Sonoma wine country: quiet roads through vineyards and redwoods, steep climbs out toward the Pacific, and plenty of dirt for gravel days.

children.name: King Ridge Road
children.note: Steep, remote climb through redwoods toward the coast

children.name: Coleman Valley Road
children.note: Steep climb up from the coast near Occidental

destinations.hireNote: A few shops in town rent high-end road and gravel bikes

destinations.name: Aspen
destinations.terrain: High mountain passes and alpine singletrack; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: High-country riding: road climbs over Independence Pass and up to the Maroon Bells, plus alpine singletrack and Snowmass's lift-served bike park.
destinations.weather: Afternoon storms in summer; Independence Pass is closed from about November to late May.

children.name: Independence Pass
children.note: ~30 km, ~1,300 m to 3,687 m on the Continental Divide

children.name: Maroon Creek Road
children.note: ~16 km to the Maroon Bells; cars restricted in the day in summer

children.name: Snowmass Bike Park
children.note: Lift-served flow and downhill

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops renting road, mountain and e-bikes

destinations.name: Woodstock (Vermont gravel)
destinations.terrain: Steep dirt roads through farms and forest; intermediate
destinations.pitch: Vermont has thousands of kilometres of unpaved town roads, steep and quiet, through farms, maple forest and covered bridges. Best in autumn colour.
destinations.weather: Mud season in April and May makes the dirt roads soft.
destinations.hireNote: A couple of shops rent gravel bikes

destinations.name: Arizona Trail
destinations.airport: Mexican border near Sierra Vista (start), Utah border (end)
destinations.terrain: Rough, rocky singletrack with hike-a-bike; advanced, very remote
destinations.pitch: Border to border across Arizona on singletrack, from saguaro desert and sky-island mountains to the pines of the north and the Grand Canyon, which you have to carry your bike across. Bikes detour around wilderness areas.
destinations.weather: Water is the main challenge: long dry stretches and caches.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for bikepacking and rough singletrack

destinations.name: Maah Daah Hey Trail
destinations.terrain: Badlands singletrack with sharp climbs; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: About 150 km of singletrack through the North Dakota badlands, past Theodore Roosevelt National Park, with campgrounds and water caches along the way.
destinations.weather: The clay trail is unrideable when wet; summer storms and heat.
destinations.hireNote: A few outfitters in Medora run supported trips

destinations.name: Oregon Timber Trail
destinations.terrain: Backcountry singletrack and forest roads; advanced
destinations.pitch: A bikepacking route from California to the Columbia River on mostly singletrack, through high desert, volcanoes and old-growth forest, past Oakridge and Mount Hood.
destinations.weather: Wildfire smoke and closures are common in late summer.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for bikepacking on singletrack

destinations.name: Katy Trail
destinations.airport: St Louis (east end); Kansas City ~1.5 h from the west end
destinations.terrain: Flat, crushed-stone rail trail; easy
destinations.pitch: America's longest continuous rail trail, along the Missouri River bluffs through small wine towns, flat and easy all the way.
destinations.weather: Summer is hot and humid; spring floods can close sections.
destinations.hireNote: A few outfitters rent bikes and run shuttles, mostly near the east end

destinations.name: Great Allegheny Passage & C&O Canal
destinations.terrain: Crushed-stone rail trail, then a rougher dirt towpath; easy
destinations.pitch: From Pittsburgh over the Eastern Continental Divide on a gentle rail trail, then down the old C&O Canal towpath along the Potomac into Washington DC.
destinations.hireNote: Outfitters at both ends and along the way rent bikes and run shuttles

destinations.name: Icefields Parkway
destinations.airport: Edmonton ~4 h to Jasper; Calgary ~1.5 h from Banff
destinations.terrain: Mountain highway with a wide shoulder; intermediate
destinations.pitch: One of the world's great mountain roads: about 230 km between Jasper and Banff past glaciers, turquoise lakes and two big passes, with hostels and lodges along the way.
destinations.weather: Snow is possible on the passes in any month, and there are bears near the road.
destinations.hireNote: Shops in Banff and Jasper rent road bikes; no one-way hire

destinations.name: Cabot Trail
destinations.terrain: Coastal road with steep climbs over the headlands; intermediate
destinations.pitch: A loop around Cape Breton's highlands, with steep climbs over coastal headlands, Gaelic and Acadian villages and whales offshore. Autumn colour peaks in early October.
destinations.hireNote: A few shops in Baddeck and Sydney; most riders bring their own

destinations.name: Blue Ridge Parkway
destinations.airport: Waynesboro, Virginia (north end), Cherokee, North Carolina (south end)
destinations.terrain: Smooth, scenic road with long climbs and no shoulder; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: A scenic road along the crest of the Appalachians, with no trucks or traffic lights, long climbs and long views, and Mount Mitchell, the highest peak east of the Mississippi, just off the route.
destinations.weather: Sections close for snow and fog in winter; there are long tunnels in the south, so carry lights.
destinations.hireNote: No one-way hire; bring your own or go with a tour company

destinations.name: Oregon Coast
destinations.airport: Astoria (start), Brookings (end); Portland ~2 h to Astoria
destinations.terrain: Coast highway with a shoulder and rolling headlands; intermediate
destinations.pitch: Ride south with the summer tailwind along the Oregon coast: sea stacks, lighthouses, dunes and seafood towns, with hiker-biker campsites in the state parks.
destinations.weather: Ride north to south in summer, when the wind is behind you.
destinations.hireNote: No one-way hire
